does.mpris.body: Track and position are read over D-Bus; nothing is installed on the player's side. Position is interpolated from a local clock rather than polled every frame.
does.sources.body: Source order, matching, fallback and the local cache are all configurable; a source with no result hands over to the next one in order.
does.through.body: With click-through on, pointer events pass to the window underneath and the lyrics stop intercepting clicks.
does.follow: Theme and language follow the system
does.follow.body: Light, dark and follow-system; the interface language can be left to the system as well. Both sit on the first page of the settings window and take effect without a restart.
does.layer.body: Needs a compositor implementing wlr-layer-shell — KDE/KWin or anything wlroots-based; GNOME/Mutter falls back to an ordinary top-most window. Frosted glass additionally needs ext-background-effect-v1 or the older org_kde_kwin_blur; with neither present the panel stays translucent and the option disables itself.
hero.title: Wayland desktop lyrics
hero.lead: Kotonoha reads MPRIS playback state over D-Bus and draws word-timed lyrics on a Wayland layer. Any player implementing MPRIS works, with nothing installed on its side.
design.title:
The site looks like the program
because the values are the same file.
design.lead: None of the colour is taken twice — every value comes from theme.py and models.py. This page records the values, the components, and which rules can go red.
s.parts.lead: One role, one implementation. They are rendered side by side because that is the only way a drifted variant shows up.
s.search.lead: When one song returns a dozen results, this window answers which. Click a header to sort — length by seconds, match by rank, neither by what the cell says.
foot.lead: A Wayland lyrics layer for the Linux desktop
foot.desc: Requires a Wayland compositor implementing wlr-layer-shell; KDE/KWin and wlroots-based compositors qualify.
get.lead: Gentoo through the gentoo-zh overlay, Arch through kotonoha-git on the AUR, NixOS through a flake, or build it from source.
